# Story 54 — In-app notifications for ticket events (Story: 54)

## Prerequisites

- **Story 10** (auto-assign a ticket to an available agent) — this story's `pickNextAvailableAgent` call site in `backend/src/routes/ticket.routes.ts` (around line 143–192) is one of two triggers that must call the new notification helper. If Story 10 has not yet been implemented in its final form, coordinate with the owner so both use the same helper name.
- **Story 12** (escalate a ticket) — the second trigger. There is no `PATCH /tickets/:id/escalate` route in `backend/src/routes/ticket.routes.ts` today (grep for `escalate` in that file returns zero matches inside handler bodies); this story only wires the notification hook into whatever route Story 12 lands on. If Story 12 is not yet built, this plan adds the notification *helper* and the *me-scoped read/mark-read endpoints and UI*, and leaves a documented `TODO` comment at the eventual escalate call site for that story's executor to satisfy.
- No prior plan files exist under `.squad/plans/ticket-management/`; this may be the first story authored in that feature folder. Update `00-overview.md` accordingly (create it if missing).

---

## Story Goal

Deliver the in-app notification mechanism promised by Stories 10 and 12:

1. A per-agent `Notification` document is written whenever a ticket is auto-assigned or escalated to that agent.
2. Every authenticated staff account can list its own unread-first notifications and mark one read, via self-scoped `me`-routes.
3. The persistent header shows an unread badge (count) on the existing bell in `frontend/components/SiteHeader.tsx`, and clicking an item routes to the linked ticket and marks it read.
4. Delivery is **polling-based**, not Socket.io. The intake explicitly permits polling and says to note the choice — this story picks polling because it satisfies "persist across sessions until read" without pulling notifications into the live-chat socket surface.

**Not in scope:** live-chat notifications, email notifications (already covered by `backend/src/services/email.service.ts`), notification preferences/settings, marking-all-as-read (single-item `PATCH .../read` only), notification deletion, admin/sub-admin notifications for anything other than ticket assignment/escalation (they'll only receive a notification if they are the `assignedAgent` or `escalatedTo` of a ticket, which is unusual but not forbidden by the model).

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current behaviour:** `frontend/components/NotificationBell.tsx` shows a bell that opens a dropdown saying "Notifications — coming soon" (line 33). No backend model, no route, no data.
- **New behaviour:** the bell shows an unread count badge when the caller has ≥1 unread notification; the dropdown lists the caller's recent notifications (unread first, then newest read), each item links to `/tickets/<ticketId>` and marks itself read on click; the badge count refreshes at least on route change and on a **60-second interval** while the tab is focused.

## Backend Tasks

### 1 — New `Notification` model

**Create file:** `backend/src/models/Notification.ts`

Mirror the shape and comment density of `backend/src/models/Message.ts`. Exact fields:

```ts
import mongoose, { Document, Schema, Types } from "mongoose";

export type NotificationType = "ticket_assigned" | "ticket_escalated";

export interface INotification extends Document {
  recipient: Types.ObjectId;      // ref User — the agent (or admin/subadmin) being notified
  type: NotificationType;
  ticketId: Types.ObjectId;       // ref Ticket — the ticket this notification is about
  read: boolean;
  createdAt: Date;
  updatedAt: Date;
}

const notificationSchema = new Schema<INotification>(
  {
    recipient: { type: Schema.Types.ObjectId, ref: "User", required: true },
    type: { type: String, enum: ["ticket_assigned", "ticket_escalated"], required: true },
    ticketId: { type: Schema.Types.ObjectId, ref: "Ticket", required: true },
    read: { type: Boolean, default: false },
  },
  { timestamps: true }
);

// Backs the two hot queries: badge count (recipient + read=false) and
// dropdown listing (recipient + createdAt desc). Mirrors Message.ts's
// compound-index approach.
notificationSchema.index({ recipient: 1, read: 1, createdAt: -1 });

export const Notification = mongoose.model<INotification>("Notification", notificationSchema);
```

Add a top-of-file comment explaining Story 54 and pointing out that live-chat's future notifications (out of scope here) will extend `NotificationType` with new string values rather than a second model.

### 2 — Notification-creation helper

**Create file:** `backend/src/services/notification.service.ts`

Exported function:

```ts
import { Types } from "mongoose";
import { Notification, type NotificationType } from "../models/Notification";

/**
 * Story 54 — write a per-recipient in-app notification. Idempotent-ish:
 * the caller decides when to invoke, and duplicate notifications for the
 * same event are acceptable (there is no unique index) because the
 * assignment / escalation call sites already guard against re-firing.
 * Never throws to the caller — a notification is a side-effect, and
 * failing to write it must not break the ticket write itself. Errors are
 * logged via console.error, matching how email.service.ts's failures are
 * currently surfaced.
 */
export async function createTicketNotification(params: {
  recipient: Types.ObjectId | string;
  type: NotificationType;
  ticketId: Types.ObjectId | string;
}): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await Notification.create({
      recipient: params.recipient,
      type: params.type,
      ticketId: params.ticketId,
    });
  } catch (err) {
    console.error("[notification.service] failed to create notification", err);
  }
}
```

### 5 — Self-scoped notification routes on `/me`

**File:** `backend/src/routes/me.routes.ts`

At the end of the file (just before `export default router;` at line 195), add two handlers. Follow the precedent comments at lines 14–21 and 33–42 — every new handler needs a paragraph explaining why it is `requireAuth`-only and self-scoped.

```ts
// GET /api/v1/me/notifications — self-read of the caller's in-app
// notification feed for Story 54. Self-scoped for the same reason as
// /me/contact above: a signed-in staff account only ever reads their own
// notifications, never another user's, so a permission key would be a
// no-op. Unread first, then most-recent read, capped at 20 items so a
// long-lived account doesn't paginate the badge dropdown.
router.get("/notifications", requireAuth, async (req: Request, res: Response) => {
  const items = await Notification.find({ recipient: req.user!.id })
    .sort({ read: 1, createdAt: -1 })
    .limit(20)
    .lean();
  const unreadCount = await Notification.countDocuments({
    recipient: req.user!.id,
    read: false,
  });
  res.status(200).json({
    unreadCount,
    items: items.map((n) => ({
      id: String(n._id),
      type: n.type,
      ticketId: String(n.ticketId),
      read: n.read,
      createdAt: n.createdAt.toISOString(),
    })),
  });
});

// PATCH /api/v1/me/notifications/:id/read — flip read=true, but only if
// the notification's recipient matches req.user!.id. Any other case
// (wrong id, someone else's notification, malformed id) is a 404 rather
// than a 403, so an attacker cannot use the difference to enumerate
// notification ids that belong to another user.
router.patch("/notifications/:id/read", requireAuth, async (req: Request, res: Response) => {
  if (!mongoose.isValidObjectId(req.params.id)) {
    res.status(404).json({ error: "Notification not found" });
    return;
  }
  const updated = await Notification.findOneAndUpdate(
    { _id: req.params.id, recipient: req.user!.id },
    { $set: { read: true } },
    { new: true }
  );
  if (!updated) {
    res.status(404).json({ error: "Notification not found" });
    return;
  }
  res.status(200).json({ id: String(updated._id), read: updated.read });
});
```

Imports to add at the top of `me.routes.ts`: `import mongoose from "mongoose";` (if not already present) and `import { Notification } from "../models/Notification";`.

**Do not** add a `requirePermission` call to either route — the intake explicitly says these are self-scoped like `/me/status` and `/me/contact`. Do not add a new permission key to `backend/src/constants/permissions.ts`.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Notification write fails after ticket save succeeds** — `createTicketNotification` swallows the error and logs it (see `notification.service.ts`). The ticket still exists and is still assigned; the agent simply doesn't see a badge for that one. Enforced by the try/catch in Backend Task §2.
- **Agent is deactivated between assignment and login** — the notification still exists, but on login `requireAuth` fails at the `/me/notifications` endpoint the same way it fails at `/me/status`; the badge never renders. No cleanup needed.
- **Ticket is later deleted (hard-delete)** — the notification row still exists and its dropdown row link resolves to a 404 ticket page. Acceptable; `frontend/app/tickets/[id]/page.tsx` already handles missing tickets. No cascade delete in this story (documented in `## Migration / Rollback`).
- **Escalation trigger is dormant** — since no `PATCH /tickets/:id/escalate` route exists in `backend/src/routes/ticket.routes.ts` today (Task §4), no `ticket_escalated` notifications will ever be written until Story 12 lands and satisfies the `TODO`. The model, the routes, and the UI all support the type; only the write-site is missing. Executor **must** verify this by grepping `escalate` in `backend/src/routes/ticket.routes.ts` before assuming a call site exists.
- **Duplicate notifications for the same event** — the schema has **no** unique index on `(recipient, type, ticketId)`. This is intentional: reassigning a ticket back to the same agent later is a legitimate second notification. The frontend does not de-dupe.
- **Cross-user id enumeration on `PATCH .../:id/read`** — the handler returns 404 for both "id doesn't exist" and "id belongs to someone else". Enforced by the combined `{ _id, recipient: req.user!.id }` filter in Task §5.
- **Malformed ObjectId in `:id`** — pre-validated with `mongoose.isValidObjectId` before hitting the DB. Enforced in Task §5.
- **Interval fetch on a background tab** — skipped via `document.hidden`. Prevents needless traffic and stops the polling loop from firing while the token silently expires; the visibility-change listener re-fires immediately on tab focus. Enforced in Frontend Task §2.
- **Customer accidentally receives a notification** — impossible under the current call sites: `assignedAgent` and `escalatedTo` are only ever set to users with `role: "agent"` by `pickNextAvailableAgent` (see `backend/src/services/assignment.service.ts` lines 32–38, filter includes `role: "agent"`). If a future manual-reassign route sets those fields to another role, that route's author is responsible for whether a notification is appropriate.
- **RTL/Arabic layout** — the badge uses logical `-end-1` positioning (not `-right-1`) so it renders correctly under `dir="rtl"`. Enforced in Frontend Task §2.

## Migration / Rollback

- **Schema addition only.** No existing collection is altered; no backfill script is needed (unlike `backfill-ticket-numbers.ts`).
- **Rollback:** drop the `notifications` collection (`db.notifications.drop()`) and revert the three code changes (model, service, `me.routes.ts` handlers, `ticket.routes.ts` call site). The bell reverts to its placeholder state by reverting `NotificationBell.tsx`.
- **Half-applied state considerations:** if the backend ships first with the `createTicketNotification` call in `ticket.routes.ts` but the frontend still shows the placeholder bell, notifications accumulate silently in Mongo — harmless. If the frontend ships first, `fetchNotifications` returns an empty list (backend endpoint 404 until Task §5 lands) — the badge simply never appears. Ship backend first to avoid the 404 case.
- **No cascade on ticket delete** — documented in edge cases. If a future story adds a hard-delete for tickets, that story owns adding a `Notification.deleteMany({ ticketId })` step.
